stage_messages.introduction: Hey Doctor! Ethan needs your help. Start with what happened, then keep your patient safe. You’ve got this!
stage_messages.history: Good questions uncover the mechanism and red flags. You do not need to ask everything—ask what changes your decisions.
stage_messages.examination: Slow and safe. Inspect first, localize tenderness and protect injured structures while checking nerves and circulation.
stage_messages.investigations: Choose the smallest clinically sufficient set of tests. I’ll show you each written report as you order it.
stage_messages.diagnosis: Now connect the mechanism, examination and investigations. Which diagnosis actually explains all three?
stage_messages.treatment: The treatment tray is shuffled. Each safe action gets its sequence number when its prerequisites are complete.
stage_messages.knowledge_check: Nice work! Three quick questions to lock in the clinical reasoning.
stage_messages.completion: Great job with Ethan! The best clinicians are careful about both decisions and patient safety.

case_specific_guidance.diagnostic_nudge: Is the tenderness medial, middle or lateral along the collarbone?
case_specific_guidance.differentiating_clue: The fracture is midshaft with mild displacement and no threatened skin.
case_specific_guidance.clinical_coaching: A closed minimally displaced midshaft clavicle fracture usually receives analgesia, simple sling, safety instructions and follow-up—not automatic fixation.
key_teaching_points: Skin compromise and neurovascular/chest symptoms change urgency.
Minimal displacement often allows sling and progressive rehab.
Adult markedly displaced fractures warrant a different shared surgical decision.
